title: RFID Manufacturer in Shenzhen — Factory-Direct
summary: Proud Tek is a Shenzhen RFID manufacturer — building in-house since 2008 and shipping to buyers in 50+ countries — that makes the full RFID product range under two factory roofs: RFID cards and fobs, NFC tags and stickers, UHF inlays and labels, event wristbands, keyfobs and the readers to run them, each assembled, laminated, encoded and 100% read-tested on ten automated lines. Sourcing from Shenzhen puts the world's densest RFID supply chain on the factory's doorstep — chip makers, antenna etchers, substrate mills and converting-equipment builders within a short drive — so a six-family program consolidates with one supplier instead of five. This page maps the full product menu with chips, MOQ and air-interface standards, what runs on the Shenzhen floor, the sample-to-PO path, and the certifications your procurement team can verify before the first order.

sections.title: Why buy RFID from a Shenzhen manufacturer
sections.intro: Shenzhen makes more of the world's RFID than any other city, and it is not an accident of branding — the chip distributors, antenna etchers, substrate suppliers and converting-machine builders sit within a short drive of each other, so a factory here sources in days what an assembler elsewhere waits weeks to import. Proud Tek has built [RFID cards](/products/rfid-cards/), [labels](/products/rfid-labels/) and [tags](/products/rfid-tags/) in that cluster since 2008, across two factories and ten automated lines, and the [factory tour](/about/factory/) is an open invitation rather than an awkward request. The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first.
bullets: Six product families under one roof — cards and fobs, NFC tags and stickers, UHF inlays and labels, event wristbands, keyfobs and readers — so a mixed RFID program consolidates with one supplier instead of five.

The Shenzhen supply chain on the doorstep: chips, antennas, PVC and PET substrates and converting equipment sourced locally, which is why sample and re-order lead times stay short even on custom parts.

Chip-vendor agnostic — we bond NXP, Infineon, Impinj, Alien, EM Microelectronic and Quanray inlays in-house, so a program is specified around your read requirement, not around whatever one distributor is pushing.

A direct factory, not a trading desk: your purchase order reaches the production planner and the engineers who build the part, at the factory-gate price, with compliance documents shipped as standard rather than billed as an extra.

Every value-added step is in-house — inlay bonding, lamination, printing, encoding, laser marking and final QC — so no subcontracted step can quietly swap a chip or a substrate between your sample and your production run.

bullets: Cards and fobs run to ISO/IEC 14443 (13.56 MHz) and ISO/IEC 11784/11785 (125 kHz LF); PVC, PET, ABS, polycarbonate, wood and recycled bodies are laminated in-house, with MIFARE Plus and DESFire key diversification written on the encoding line.

NFC stickers and tags use NTAG 213, NTAG 215 and NTAG 216 for URL, vCard and marketing taps, and NTAG 424 DNA when a label must prove it is genuine with AES-128 SUN authentication; ICODE SLIX2 covers HF vicinity work to ISO/IEC 15693.
UHF inlays and labels use Impinj and NXP UCODE silicon to ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2v2 (860-960 MHz), encoded to the GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard for retail and logistics.

The MOQs above are typical starting points; the firm minimum depends on chip, size, finish and encoding, so we quote it in writing per program rather than post one number that is wrong for half of them.

sections.title: What runs on the Shenzhen floor
sections.intro: A manufacturer should be able to show you the machines, not just the catalogue. Production runs across two Shenzhen sites and ten automated lines organised into six line families — every value-added step happens here, and the operators who build your pilot lot are the same people who run the production order, which is why first-run defect rates tend to stay flat across a program's life. Browse the finished parts on the [RFID tags](/products/rfid-tags/) and [wristbands](/products/rfid-wristbands/) catalogues, or see the plant itself on the [factory page](/about/factory/).

image.alt: A left-to-right factory-floor flow in six stages. Stage 1, materials in: chips, antennas and PVC and PET substrates sourced locally in Shenzhen. Stage 2, inlay bonding: chip-to-antenna for HF 13.56 MHz and UHF 860-960 MHz inlays at ESD-controlled stations. Stage 3, lamination and print: PVC, ABS and PET stocks laminated, offset and screen printing, laser marking. Stage 4, encoding: UID locking, NDEF, GS1 SGTIN-96 and MIFARE Plus and DESFire keys. Stage 5, QC: 100% functional read test plus AQL visual and dimensional sampling. Stage 6, export packing: FOB, CIF or DDP shipping to 50+ countries. A footer notes every value-added step is in-house across two Shenzhen sites and ten automated lines.

bullets: Wet-inlay assembly — chip-to-antenna bonding for HF (13.56 MHz) and UHF (860-960 MHz) inlays on PET and PI substrates, at ESD-controlled stations with readability QC at the line.
Card and label lamination — PVC, ABS, PETG, recycled-PVC and transparent stocks hot-roll laminated, with inlay placement held tight enough for reproducible MIFARE Plus and DESFire encoding.
Anti-metal lamination — ferrite-backed inlays for on-metal asset, tool and equipment tags, with read range validated against steel and aluminium surfaces per SKU.
Encoding and personalisation — UID locking, NDEF programming, GS1 SGTIN-96, key diversification and reel-to-reel encoding for high-volume UHF programs, 100% read-verified before packing.
Print and marking — four-colour offset, screen printing, hot stamping, laser engraving for consecutive serialisation, and variable-data inkjet for QR and barcode overlays.
Final QC, packaging and warehouse — 100% functional read test on every encoded unit, AQL sampling on visual and dimensional attributes, and bonded warehousing for distributor safety stock.

sections.title: From free sample to a standing PO
sections.intro: Nobody should wire a deposit for a tag they have not held. The path below front-loads the cheap, reversible steps — a [free sample pack](/sample-pack/) first, a small pilot second, and a locked-price production run only once the parts read cleanly on your own equipment. A mixed program can then consolidate the [China RFID card manufacturer](/lp/rfid-card-manufacturer-china/) and [RFID label manufacturer](/lp/rfid-label-manufacturer/) lines under one purchase order.

faq.question: How do I verify Proud Tek is a real Shenzhen factory and not a trading company?
faq.answer: Three independent checks. Request our ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificate numbers and confirm them with the issuing registrar — they name the manufacturing entity, not a trading name. Book a factory audit across our two Shenzhen sites, in person or by live video walk-through, with third-party (SGS, TUV, Intertek) inspection when your program requires it. Then order a sample pack and put the parts on your own readers. A trading company cannot pass all three, because it owns no line to show you.

faq.question: Which RFID products can one Shenzhen manufacturer actually make in-house?
faq.answer: All six families on this page: RFID cards and fobs, NFC tags and stickers, UHF inlays and labels, event wristbands, keyfobs, and desktop, handheld and fixed RFID readers. Inlay bonding, lamination, printing, encoding and QC all happen on our own lines, which is what lets a buyer consolidate a mixed program — cards plus labels plus wristbands — with a single supplier and one point of accountability.

faq.question: How does buying direct from the Shenzhen factory compare with a trading company?
faq.answer: You pay the factory-gate price instead of that price plus a reseller's margin — a trading company typically adds 15-30% for handling the transaction while owning no line to inspect an inlay, retune an antenna or expedite a run. Buying direct puts the engineering, quality and production-planning teams on the other end of your email, and makes one party accountable when a batch has to be reworked.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity, and can I test first?
faq.answer: Free samples come first: we ship 8-12 encoded SKUs so you qualify the part before committing. For production, typical minimums start around 500 pieces for RFID cards, keyfobs and wristbands and 1,000 pieces for NFC stickers, labels and inlays, kept low because we hold running stock of popular chips and materials. The firm MOQ depends on chip, size, finish and encoding, so we quote it in writing per program; specialty substrates such as anti-metal or custom shapes carry higher minimums for dedicated tooling.

faq.question: What payment terms do you offer international buyers?
faq.answer: First orders typically run 50% deposit and 50% balance before shipment by T/T, with PayPal and Alibaba Trade Assurance available on samples and small orders so a new buyer has payment protection. Established distributors and brand-owner programs move onto open-account terms (Net 30 / Net 60) after the first one or two orders, with Letter-of-Credit support for higher volumes. Exact terms are confirmed in writing per order alongside the quote.
